stories.title: Body of King Oyo returns to Uganda ahead of burial
stories.summary: Mouners gathered at Entebbe airport on Friday to receive the body of Uganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV. He died of an undisclosed illness last week in the United States at the age of 34. President Yoweri Museveni received the casket in a formal military parade. "I gave assistance to the king and his family before his death. They first went to Germany and later they went to United States for treatment but it didn’t go as we hoped." King Oyo ascended to the throne of Uganda’s Tooro kingdom at three years old and held the unofficial title of the world’s youngest reigning monarch. “In fact this is unbearable," said Rwomusha Ibanda Gerald, a Tooro prince. "It was shocking to lose a wonderful and impactful king. He has died at age of 34 but impactful, someone might die of 90, 80 but with little records but at 34 years the record is immense." Uganda is a republic but officially recognises traditional kingdoms. They have limited political power but their monarchs wield authority as guardians of tribal culture. Oyo was not officially married when he died and there are fears his death could trigger a succession crisis.

stories.title: 'Major potential breaches of British election law': Understanding Channel 4's investigation
stories.summary: Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Peter Geoghegan, a multi-award-winning investigative journalist. He's the editor of the Substack Democracy for Sale and the author of the best-selling book Democracy for Sale. Geoghegan explains the significance of the Channel 4 investigation not simply in the conduct allegedly captured on camera, but in the broader question of how political influence is financed and made visible, or invisible, within British democracy.
